description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4, `comp/` CHECK 2).  PRE-EXISTING.  This is the
single biggest attributed cluster in `comp/`.

perl's `require` (and `do FILE`, and `use`) evaluates the file and takes the
value of its LAST statement:
  * a FALSE value is the fatal `"NAME did not return a true value"` -- which is
    why every module ends `1;`;
  * a TRUE value is `require`'s own return value;
  * under `use feature 'module_true'` (perl 5.38+, and on by default from
    `use v5.38`), a module needs no trailing true value and require answers a
    plain 1.

PCL answers 1 unconditionally and never raises the fatal.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl), four one-line modules in the cwd, `@INC`
including ".", `%INC` cleared between:

    mtA.pm  "package mtA; sub foo {}; 7;"
    mtB.pm  "package mtB; sub foo {}; 0;"
    mtC.pm  "package mtC; use feature 'module_true'; sub foo {};"
    mtD.pm  ""                                 (empty file)

                     perl                               PCL
    require mtA.pm   rv=7                               rv=1
    require mtB.pm   rv=undef, $@ "mtB.pm did not        rv=1, $@ empty
                     return a true value at ..."
    require mtC.pm   rv=1                               rv=1
    require mtD.pm   rv=undef, $@ "mtD.pm did not ..."   rv=1, $@ empty
    list context     (7)                                (1)

WHAT IT COSTS (measured, `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 --timeout 450`,
this tree): t/comp/require.t DIFF 911/836 of 1750 perl rows.  Its 500 logged
fail rows (the file is over the #1051 log cap, so the multiset is PARTIAL)
cluster as:
    119  (BB) saw expected error                 -- `$err =~ /did not return a true value/`
     76  (AB) scalar return value is simple true value <N>
     76  (AB) list return value is simple true value <N>
     42  (BA) ... should die                     -- the fatal itself
     40  (CB) returned expected value
    ~140 (AA) `use feature ...` / `module_true` singles, same generated matrix
so ~353 of the 500 are directly this fact and most of the rest are the same
generated loop (require.t builds mttestNNN.pm files from a cross product of
`use feature ':5.38' / ':all' / 'module_true' / v5.38 / no feature` x
`return 0 / (0, return 0) / no trailing value` x six call spellings).

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (why it is not a one-hour fix): PCL compiles a module to a
CL file and caches it, and the module-load path (`p-require-file` + the
cache) has no notion of "the file's last expression value".  The value has to
survive the CACHED path too (#1303's cache dir; the generation key), or the
answer would depend on whether the module was compiled this run -- which is
exactly the class of bug `docs/DECIDED.md` §s403 names ("a diagnostic that can
fire during a RUN must answer 'and on a warm cache?'").  `module_true` is the
modern default, so the FATAL half is the part real CPAN code depends on.

Three of require.t's rows are SHORTFALL rather than fail rows (911+836 = 1747
of 1750) and are not attributed here; they need their own reading.
subject: `require` always answers 1 and never enforces "did not return a true value": a module's OWN last value is not its require's value -- t/comp/require.t's ~353 of 500 blessed fail rows are this one fact
